subject.title: [Bug]: The project won't start on Windows and WSL.

question: Should this Windows/WSL second-build hang be treated as beta-blocking tsdown rollback/pin/update work now, or should maintainers require a current-main Windows/WSL repro log before choosing the fix direction?
rationale: The report is credible and affects a supported setup path, but automation cannot safely choose a broad tsdown-to-tsc rollback or dependency strategy without live platform proof and maintainer intent.

options.title: Require focused repro first
options.body: Ask for or run current-main native Windows and WSL first-build/second-build logs before deciding between dependency update, pin, wrapper fix, or rollback.

options.title: Treat as beta-blocking now
options.body: Promote this to a beta-blocking build investigation and let maintainers choose a temporary pin or rollback while repro proof is gathered.

options.title: Wait for reporter detail
options.body: Keep the issue open with a needs-info posture until the reporter provides exact logs, version, install method, and whether WSL or native Windows is affected.

recommendation.title: Require focused repro first
recommendation.body: Ask for or run current-main native Windows and WSL first-build/second-build logs before deciding between dependency update, pin, wrapper fix, or rollback.

likelyOwner.reason: The most direct recent history for Windows tsdown process-tree handling points to vincentkoc.
